questions.solution_html:
• Principal Point in Aerial Photograph: The point where the camera’s optical axis
  • intersects the photograph, can be identified with the help of fiducial marks (1
  • mark). It represents the geometric centre of the photograph ((1 mark)).

questions.question: Effects of Rayleigh Scattering.
questions.solution_html:
• Effects of Rayleigh Scattering.
  • Shorter wavelengths scatter more strongly ((1 mark)), making the sky appear blue.
  • It causes haze in the remote sensing data products ((1 mark)).

questions.question: Zone Delineation.
questions.solution_html:
• Zone Delineation.
  • Zone delineation in GIS is the process of defining boundaries that divide geographic
  • space into meaningful areas or zones. A zone is a spatial area enclosed by a
  • boundary in which features tend to have similar characteristics ((1 mark)). For
  • example, Hydrological Zones is an example, which include Watersheds, Sub
  • watersheds, Drainage basins, Riparian zones, Flood-prone areas etc. ((1 mark)).
questions.final_answer: watersheds, Drainage basins, Riparian zones, Flood-prone areas etc. ()
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: ERDAS Imagine.

questions.question: Role of GCP in georeferencing.
questions.solution_html:
• Role of GCP in georeferencing.
  • Ground Control Points (GCPs) are identifiable locations with known ground
  • coordinates ((1 mark)). They are used to align satellite imagery or aerial
  • photographs with a map coordinate system, ensuring accurate spatial positioning
  • and reducing geometric distortions ((1 mark)).
questions.final_answer: and reducing geometric distortions ()
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Quantitative Mapping.
questions.solution_html:
• Quantitative mapping
  • Quantitative mapping is the graphical representation of numerical geographical
  • data, such as population, rainfall, temperature and mineral distribution, using
  • proportional symbols, choropleth maps, dot maps and isolines (Marks 2).
questions.final_answer: proportional symbols, choropleth maps, dot maps and isolines (Marks 2)

questions.question: Compare the uses of Mirror Stereoscope and Pocket Stereoscope.
questions.solution_html:
• Mirror Stereoscope and Pocket Stereoscope ((8 Marks))
  • • Definition – (1 mark): Instruments used to view overlapping aerial photographs in 3D.
  • • Mirror stereoscope – (2 marks): Uses mirrors and prisms; provides a wider viewing area and
  • supports detailed interpretation.
  • • Pocket stereoscope – (2 marks): Uses two lenses; portable, inexpensive and suitable for quick
  • observations.
  • • Comparison – (2 marks): Mirror type is larger and suited to detailed work; pocket type is
  • compact with a limited viewing area.
  • • Conclusion – (1 mark): Both are useful in photogrammetry and terrain interpretation.
questions.final_answer: • Conclusion – : Both are useful in photogrammetry and terrain interpretation
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain Map Projection. Describe the types of projections. / Describe Overlay Analysis. Explain its importance in GIS-based spatial
questions.solution_html:
• Map Projection and Types ((8 Marks))
  • • Definition – (2 marks): Mathematical transformation of the curved Earth onto a flat map
  • inevitably introducing distortions.
  • • Cylindrical projection – (1.5 marks): Uses a cylinder; useful for world maps and navigation.
  • • Conical projection – (1.5 marks): Uses a cone; suitable for middle-latitude regions.
  • • Azimuthal projection – (1.5 marks): Uses a plane; useful for polar regions and directional
  • mapping.
  • • Properties and applications – (1.5 marks): Conformal preserves angles, equal-area preserves
  • area, and equidistant preserves selected distances.
questions.final_answer: area, and equidistant preserves selected distances
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: / analysis.
questions.solution_html:
• Overlay Analysis in GIS ((8 Marks))
  • • Definition – (2 marks): Combines multiple spatial layers to identify relationships and patterns.
  • • Types – (2 marks): Vector overlay, raster overlay and weighted overlay.
  • • Procedure – (1 mark): Prepare datasets, align coordinate systems, select layers and perform
  • overlay.
  • • Applications – (2 marks): Site selection, groundwater potential, landslide zonation and land
  • use planning.
  • • Limitations and conclusion – (1 mark): Accuracy depends on input data quality, resolution and
  • appropriate weighting.
questions.final_answer: appropriate weighting
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: / applications in geospatial studies.
questions.solution_html:
• GPS: Principles, Components and Applications ((12 Marks))
  • • Introduction – (1 mark): GPS is a satellite-based positioning, navigation and timing system.
  • • Basic principles – (3 marks): Satellite signals, travel-time measurement, trilateration and use of
  • at least four satellites for standard 3D positioning with clock correction.
  • • Major components – (3 marks)
  • o Space segment – (1 mark)
  • o Control segment – (1 mark)
  • o User segment – (1 mark)
  • • Applications – (4 marks): Surveying, GIS mapping, geological mapping, remote sensing
  • disaster management, precision agriculture and crustal deformation monitoring.
  • • Conclusion and limitations – (1 mark): GPS improves spatial data collection; atmospheric
  • errors, multipath and signal obstruction can reduce accuracy.
questions.final_answer: errors, multipath and signal obstruction can reduce accuracy
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the applications of GIS in Urban Planning and Management.
questions.solution_html:
• Applications of GIS in Urban Planning and Management ((12 Marks))
  • • Introduction – (1 mark): GIS collects, manages, analyses and displays spatial data for urban
  • planning.
  • • Land-use planning – (2 marks): Zoning, urban expansion monitoring
questions.final_answer: • Land-use planning – : Zoning, urban expansion monitoring
